hero.title: Learn mobile
hero.lede: I’m Gabriel Moro. I write, record and speak about what I learn while building Android, Kotlin Multiplatform and Flutter apps — less abstract theory, more real decisions and examples you can apply to your own project.
hero.portraitAlt: Portrait of Gabriel Moro, smiling and wearing glasses.

about.heading: What I learn in code, I share here.
paragraphs: I’ve worked in mobile since 2017 — today with Flutter and the VTEX ecosystem at Kobe. Along the way I learned that the most useful lessons come from real projects: architecture, testing, Kotlin Multiplatform and the routine of keeping code alive.

I write, record and speak to give back what I learn. The idea is simple: less abstract theory, more engineering context, examples and trade-offs you can adapt to your own project — no magic shortcuts.

content.heading: What I learn, I write down.
content.lede: Technical writing on Android, Kotlin Multiplatform, architecture and mobile careers — written from real decisions, not abstract theory.

experience.heading: Where I learned what I share.
experience.lede: Projects and teams that shaped how I work. Full history on LinkedIn.

roles.title: Senior Mobile Engineer
bullets: Building and evolving mobile e-commerce apps with Flutter and Dart, from discovery to delivery.
Architecture, automated tests and engineering practices so the team can ship with confidence.
VTEX ecosystem integration, code reviews and knowledge sharing across the team.

roles.title: Senior Mobile Engineer
bullets: Core features for a cash-back app with millions of users and daily transactions.
Took part in adopting Kotlin Multiplatform (Compose Multiplatform) and supported developers through the transition.
Feature flags, CI/CD with linting, Maestro UI tests and architecture standards.

roles.title: Senior Android Engineer
bullets: Android features for a carrier app used by millions of people.
Hilt, Jetpack Compose and multi-module projects in a large-scale product.

roles.title: Senior Android Engineer
bullets: Android features for an enterprise recording and livestreaming app.
HD local recording, low-latency capture and a dynamic multi-participant display.
WebRTC, Dagger and Jetpack Components in a live production product.
